title: SECOND PROPERTY TAX PAYMENT DUE
full_story:
The second installment of the 2025 payable 2026 Real Estate Tax Bill is due in 2 weeks on Friday, November 20th.  If you have questions about your tax bill, please feel free to call the Treasurer’s office.  If you cannot get through, please leave a message, and they will return your call as soon as possible.  Phone 618-665-3727.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.

At the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money order.  Bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00 am to 4:00 pm Monday through Friday but closed on national holidays.

Online by credit/debit card: Go to www.govpaynow.com PLC #a00082.

Or by drop box at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

title: RETABULATION OF BLAIR PRECINCT
full_story:
The Clay County Clerk’s Office has announced it will conduct a post-election retabulation and official canvass for the November 3rd General Election.

County Clerk Amy Britton issued a memorandum stating that the Illinois State Board of Elections randomly selected the Blair precinct for retabulation.  The county is also required to test its early voting equipment, specifically the Freedom Vote Scan Tabulator number 43102, which handles all early voting precincts.

The retabulation process will take place at the County Clerk’s office on Monday, November 16th, starting at 10:00 am.  Following the retabulation, election officials will count any valid, late-returned mail-in ballots and run the official election canvass, which is expected to begin at approximately 11:00 am.

title: CLAY CITY ACCIDENT
full_story:
A late afternoon crash in Clay City sent two people to the hospital Wednesday and briefly shut down a the highway.

Illinois State Police Troop 9 responded to a two-vehicle collision at the intersection of US 50 and South Main Street in Clay City at approximately 4:35 pm.

First responders transported two individuals to area hospitals with unspecified injuries.

The crash forced authorities to close US 50 for about 45 minutes while crews cleared the scene.  State Police say the investigation is preliminary and no further information is available at this time.

title: VETERANS BREAKFASTS
full_story:
Clay County Schools will be honoring Veterans on Monday, and Tuesday.

The Flora School District will be hosting its annual Veterans’ Day program on Monday, November 9th.  There will be breakfast at 8:15 am in the Flora High School Commons for all veterans and their families.  A program, open to anyone in the community, will follow in the Conley Gymnasium.  The program will consist of performances by elementary, junior high, and high school students and a keynote address by a local veterans.  Everyone is invited to honor the dedication and service of our veterans.  Please call 618-662-2412 to let the school know how many will be attending the breakfast so proper arrangements can be made.

North Clay Unit 25 will also be having a Veterans Day program on Tuesday, November 10th.  The Veterans Breakfast will be served at 8 am in the North Clay Commons.  To make reservations for breakfast call Kali Carroll at 618-665-3393 extension 135 or email [email protected] so proper arrangements can be made.  The Veterans program will be at 9 am in the Clay County State Bank Arena.

Clay City Schools will hold a Veterans Day breakfast and assembly on Monday, November 9th.  All veterans and their families are invited to join the festivities for breakfast from 7:45 to 8:45 am with a program to follow at 9 am.  To confirm your attendance, please call the Clay City Schools at 618-676-1431.

Cisne FFA plans to honor local Veterans during their 2nd Veterans Day Breakfast on Monday from 7:30-9:30 am at the Cisne Community Center.  The complimentary breakfast includes pancakes, sausage, scrambled eggs, fruit-salad, biscuits & gravy, coffee, juice, milk.  They Welcome Wayne and Clay County Veterans and encourage them to bring family or guests.  Learn more by calling or texting Mikkie Hearle at 618-516-3371.

title: FRAN CARTER SCHOLARSHIP FASHION SHOW
full_story:
The Frontier Community College Foundation and Carnaby Square, Fairfield’s “Fashion Leader” are once again teaming up to host the 9th Annual Fran Carter Memorial Scholarship Fashion Show on Sunday.

This event is being held at First Christian Church in Fairfield.  “All three entities were close to Fran’s heart, so it is fitting that the church work with the Foundation and Carnaby Square to host the event.”  Doors will open at 2 pm, with the fashion show beginning at 2:30 pm.  Those coming to the fashion show are asked to bring canned goods.

The fashion show highlights fall fashions available exclusively at Carnaby Square as well as tuxedos available for rental.  All tickets must be purchased in advance.  Reserved tables of 8 sell for $100 and individual tickets are available for $15 each.  Drinks and light refreshments will be served.  Tickets can be purchased exclusively at Carnaby Square or through Linda Spicer who can be reached at 217-725-1340.  All proceeds will go the Fran Carter Memorial Scholarship available to second-year student athletes at Frontier.

title: PLEADS GUILTY
full_story:
Thirty-three-year-old Dakota M. Czerwonka of Montrose entered a guilty plea in court last week, admitting to one count each of grooming and sexual exploitation of a child, both Class 4 felonies, along with three Class 2 felony counts of child pornography.  As part of a plea agreement, seven additional Class 2 felony child pornography counts were dismissed.

Czerwonka, who founded and taught at Crossroads Montessori School in Effingham, was initially arrested on January 9th following a police tip regarding inappropriate electronic messages sent to a student.

Records show that Czerwonka was ordered to undergo a sex offender evaluation and he will remain in custody, pending the sentencing.  A status hearing has been scheduled for December 3rd.

title: FF VET PARADE
full_story:
Everyone is invited to The Veterans Day Parade tomorrow at 2 in downtown Fairfield.

Veterans and spouses are welcome to enjoy breakfast from 7 until 9 at the St. Edwards Catholic Church in Fairfield.  The Flag raising ceremony, National Anthem by Elizabeth Scarbough and a patriotic concert by The Roasted Chestnuts featuring Bruce Dickey on tuba begins at 1 in Freedom Park.  The parade line up will also begin at 1pm on North First Street in front of the Fairfield High Rise.

There is no need to register for parade entry, just show up and help honor our local veterans.  The 2026 Veterans Day Parade begins at 2 in downtown Fairfield.  Look for the WNOI Swag-N-Wagon, a new 2026 Jeep Wrangler Sahara with the military-inspired ’41 Olive Drab Green color.  It will feature our famous bubble blasts and our new 5ft tall “Stream in’ Eagle” riding on top.  WNOI will be handing out patriotic candy and our WNOI/Sherwin Williams Youth Sunglasses during the parade route.

title: OPERATION CHRISTMAS CHILD
full_story:
Nearly 5,000 drop-off locations for Operation Christmas Child will open soon.

According to a news release, volunteers across the country will be preparing to collect shoeboxes for this year’s Operation Christmas Child, one of the projects of Samaritan’s Purse.  Over the last 33 years, the project has collected and delivered shoeboxes filled with toys, school supplies, and personal care items to millions of children around the world.  Many of those children are suffering from war, poverty, disease and disaster.

For those who wish to participate in this year’s project, you can find a step-by-step guide on the How to Pack a Shoebox the link in this story Operation Christmas Child.  The project partners with different churches across the world to deliver the boxes once they’ve been collected. You can also donate $10 per shoebox gift online through “Follow Your Box” to receive a tracking label and discover its destination.

“Shoebox gifts may seem simple, but they have an eternal impact.  Each box is an opportunity to tell a boy or girl in need about the true meaning of Christmas,” said Franklin Graham, president of Samaritan’s Purse.  “I’ve delivered these boxes around the world, and I never get tired of seeing the joy that they bring, even in the midst of disasters, war, and poverty.”

Operation Christmas Child has collected and delivered more than 244 million gift-filled shoeboxes and delivered them to children in more than 175 countries and territories.

Collection week is set for November 16 through November 23rd.  In Flora the drop off location is Christ’s Church, packages will be collected Monday, November 16th from 1 to 3 pm and from 5 to 7 pm.  On Tuesday November 17th from 9 to 11 am, Wednesday, November 18th from 1 to 3 pm, Thursday, November 19th from 9 to 11am, Friday, November 20th from 1 to 3 pm and from 5 to 7 pm, on Saturday, November 21st from 10 to Noon, on Sunday, November 22nd from 9:30 am to 1:30 pm and on Monday, November 23rd from 7 to 9 am.

title: ALPLM GETTYSBURG ADDRESS
full_story:
An original edition of the Gettysburg Address will go on display for a limited time this month at the Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum (ALPLM), the only place in America where the public can regularly see Lincoln’s most famous speech written in his own hand.

The speech will be displayed through November 22nd.  To give more people the opportunity to experience seeing the document, admission to the museum will be free on November 19th, the 163rd anniversary of Lincoln delivering the speech at a military cemetery in Gettysburg, PA.

Admission will also be free for veterans on November 11th to mark Veterans Day.

The ALPLM will present a version of the address for people with visual impairments starting November 17th, letting them feel raised lettering and push buttons to trigger descriptions and information about the speech.  ALPLM historians will host free Q&A sessions exploring the history and lasting impact of the Gettysburg Address at 11 am and 1:30 pm on November 18th, 19th and 20th.

The Gettysburg Address is one of the most famous speeches ever given.  Its stirring prose and historic impact have been studied by everyone from schoolchildren to scholars.

“In just a few short minutes, Abraham Lincoln offered the nation a path forward, one dedicated to liberty and equality,” said Christina Shutt, executive director of the Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum.  “Seeing his carefully crafted words in his own handwriting reminds us that liberty and unity are not abstract ideals.  They are responsibilities we inherit and must protect.”

Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address on November 19th, 1863, at the dedication of a national cemetery for the thousands of Union soldiers killed at the Battle of Gettysburg.  It opens with the famous phrase “Four score and seven years ago” and finishes by describing the Civil War as a battle to preserve government “of the people, by the people, for the people.”

Only five handwritten copies of the Gettysburg Address still exist.  In addition to the ALPLM’s copy, one is in the White House, one is at Cornell University and two are at the Library of Congress.  Those institutions rarely exhibit their copies to the general public.  The ALPLM, however, displays its copy each year around the anniversary of Lincoln delivering the speech.

Also at the museum during the display of the address is the special exhibit, “The Second American Revolution.”  It traces the efforts to rebuild America after the Civil War to match Lincoln’s vision and then document the backlash that gave rise to Jim Crow laws and decades of oppression.  It includes historic pieces such as the pen Lincoln used to sign the Emancipation Proclamation, Ku Klux Klan paraphernalia, and a chair from Ford’s Theatre, where Lincoln was assassinated.

For those unable to visit in person, the ALPLM’s website offers an interactive, in-depth look at the Gettysburg Address, its history, and how it differs from other versions.  The site also provides educational resources for teachers and parents, a photo gallery, and links to additional information: www.PresidentLincoln.Illinois.gov/GettysburgAddress.

The State of Illinois has owned this edition of the address, known as the Everett Copy, since 1944, when the state’s children helped raise money to buy it from private owners.
